text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.23% today to close at $137.35, continuing a strong two-week rally of 6.05%. The stock has risen five of the last six trading days as oil prices have remained elevated—US crude is trading at $97.26 per barrel, well above historical norms—driven by escalating Middle East tensions, including Saudi Arabia's closure of its East-West pipeline after drone attacks and Iran's hardening stance against negotiations despite U.S. pressure.

The broader context is a clash between bullish and bearish forces on oil prices. While Trump's comments Friday about a potential end to Iran tensions and subsequent oil price declines spooked markets, the underlying supply disruptions and geopolitical risk remain real enough to keep crude above $97, which benefits an integrated oil producer like ConocoPhillips that profits when prices rise.
